items.title: Section: Seeds Give Rise to Experience, Experience Deposits New Seeds — The Third Aspect in Full

items.zh: 為緣性轉相？謂阿賴耶識與諸轉識作二緣性。一、為彼種子故；二、為彼所依故。為種子者，謂所有善、不善、無記轉識轉時，一切皆用阿賴耶識為種子故。為所依者，謂由阿賴耶識執受色根，五種識身依之而轉，非無執受。又由有阿賴耶識故，得有末那；由此末那為依止故，意識得轉。譬如依止眼等五根，五識身轉，非無五根。意識亦爾，非無意根。復次，諸轉識與阿賴耶識作二緣性。一、於現法中，能長養彼種子故；二、於後法中，為彼得生攝殖彼種子故。於現法中，長養彼種子者，謂如依止阿賴耶識善、不善、無記轉識轉時，如是如是於一依止同生同滅，熏習阿賴耶識；由此因緣，後後轉識善、不善、無記性，轉更增長、轉更熾盛、轉更明了而轉。於後法中，為彼得生攝殖彼種子者，謂彼熏習種類，能引攝當來異熟無記阿賴耶識。如是為彼種子故，為彼所依故，長養種子故，攝殖種子故，應知建立阿賴耶識與諸轉識互為緣性轉相。
items.en:
First, the store-consciousness serving as condition for the active consciousnesses; first, listing. The store-consciousness serves the active consciousnesses as two kinds of condition: first, as their seed-cause; second, as their basis.
Second, explaining; first, as seed-cause. As seed-cause means that whenever any wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral active consciousness arises, it invariably uses the store-consciousness as its seed.
Second, as basis; first, through appropriation. As basis means that because the store-consciousness appropriates the physical sense faculties, the five sense-consciousnesses depend upon it in order to operate; it is not the case that they operate without such appropriation.
Second, through the existence of manas; first, stating the principle. Also, because the store-consciousness exists, manas comes to exist; because manas serves as basis, the mental consciousness is able to operate.
Second, the simile applied. Just as the five sense-consciousnesses depend on the five physical faculties in order to operate, and do not operate without them, so too does the mental consciousness depend on its own mental faculty.
Second, the active consciousnesses serving as condition for the store-consciousness; first, listing. Furthermore, the active consciousnesses serve the store-consciousness as two kinds of condition: first, in this present life, nurturing its seeds; second, for a future life, planting the seeds for its own arising.
Second, explaining; first, nurturing seeds. Nurturing seeds in the present life means that whenever a wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral active consciousness arises in dependence on the store-consciousness, it arises and perishes together with it in that same instant, habituating the store-consciousness; by this cause, subsequent active consciousnesses of that same moral nature grow ever more increased, more intense, and more pronounced.
Second, planting seeds. Planting seeds for a future life means that this habituated kind is able to bring about a future ripened, neutral store-consciousness.
Second, concluding the essential meaning. Through serving as seed-cause, through serving as basis, through nurturing seeds, and through planting seeds, one should understand the establishment of the store-consciousness's own mutual causal relationship with the active consciousnesses.

items.title: Section: The Fourth Aspect Opens — Why Manas Never Leaves the Store-Consciousness's Side, Even in Deepest Meditation

items.zh: 云何建立阿賴耶識與轉識等俱轉轉相？謂阿賴耶識，或於一時唯與一種轉識俱轉，所謂末那。何以故？由此末那，我見慢等恒共相應思量行相，若有心位、若無心位，常與阿賴耶識一時俱轉，緣阿賴耶識以為境界，執我起慢思量行相。
items.en:
Fourth, the aspect of co-arising with active consciousnesses; first, posing the question. How is the store-consciousness's co-arising with the active consciousnesses established?
Second, explaining; first, distinguishing characteristics individually; first, the store-consciousness's co-arising with other consciousnesses; first, distinguishing co-arising; first, consciousnesses co-arising; first, showing this overall; first, co-arising with just one; first, stating. The store-consciousness sometimes co-arises, at a given time, with only a single active consciousness, namely manas.
Second, posing the question. Why is this?
Third, explaining. Because manas constantly corresponds with the view of self, pride, and the rest in its characteristic activity of thinking and measuring, whether in a state with active mental consciousness or without it, it constantly co-arises together with the store-consciousness at the same time, taking the store-consciousness as its object, grasping a self and giving rise to pride in its own characteristic activity of thinking and measuring.

items.title: Section: From Two Consciousnesses to All Seven — Every Combination the Store-Consciousness Can Co-Arise With

items.zh: 或於一時與二俱轉，謂末那及意識。或於一時與三俱轉，謂五識身隨一轉時。或於一時與四俱轉。謂五識身隨二轉時。或時乃至與七俱轉，謂五識身和合轉時。
items.en:
Second, co-arising with two. Sometimes it co-arises, at a given time, with two: manas and the mental consciousness.
Third, co-arising with three. Sometimes it co-arises with three, when any one of the five sense-consciousnesses is active.
Fourth, co-arising with four. Sometimes it co-arises with four, when any two of the five sense-consciousnesses are active.
Fifth, co-arising with up to seven. Sometimes it co-arises with as many as seven, when all five sense-consciousnesses are active together.

items.title: Section: "Bound by Appearances" Until Manas Itself Is Transformed, and Four Kinds of Solitary Mental Consciousness

items.zh: 又復意識，染污末那以為依止，彼未滅時，相了別縛不得解脫；末那滅已，相縛解脫。又復意識，能緣他境及緣自境。緣他境者，謂緣五識身所緣境界，或頓不頓。緣自境者，謂緣法境。
items.en:
Second, examining the mental consciousness specifically; first, distinguishing purity and defilement. The mental consciousness also takes the defiled manas as its basis; while manas remains unextinguished, it is bound by appearances and cannot attain liberation; once manas is extinguished, this bondage by appearances is released.
Commentary: as for being bound by appearances — the Establishment of Consciousness-Only Treatise says: such a defiled mind is what consciousness depends upon; while this mind remains unextinguished, consciousness's bondage can never be released.
Second, distinguishing its objects; first, stating. The mental consciousness is also able to cognize another's object and to cognize its own object.
Second, explaining; first, cognizing another's object. Cognizing another's object means cognizing the objects belonging to the five sense-consciousnesses, whether all at once or one at a time.
Second, cognizing its own object. Cognizing its own object means taking mental phenomena themselves as its object.

items.title: Section: Why Even a Hell-Being's Agony Cannot Disturb the Store-Consciousness's Own Constant Equanimity

items.zh: 復次，阿賴耶識，或於一時與苦受、樂受、不苦不樂受俱時而轉，此受與轉識相應，依彼而起。謂於人中，若欲界天，若於一分鬼、傍生中，俱生不苦不樂受，與轉識相應苦受、樂受、不苦不樂受相雜俱轉。若那落迦等中，他所映奪，不苦不樂受與純苦無雜受俱時而轉。當知此受被映奪故，難可了知。如那落迦等中，一向苦受俱轉；如是於下三靜慮地，一向樂受俱轉；於第四靜慮地乃至有頂，一向不苦不樂受俱轉。
items.en:
Second, feelings co-arising; first, stating overall. Furthermore, the store-consciousness sometimes co-arises with an active consciousness's own painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling; this feeling corresponds to and arises from that active consciousness.
Second, distinguishing individually; first, mixed co-arising. Among humans, desire-realm gods, and one portion of hungry ghosts and animals, the innate neutral feeling co-arises mixed together with an active consciousness's own painful, pleasant, or neutral feeling.
Second, exclusive co-arising; first, presenting painful feeling; first, stating exclusive co-arising. In the hell realms and the like, the neutral feeling, eclipsed by that other feeling, co-arises together with purely painful, unmixed feeling.
Second, explaining why it is hard to recognise. Know that because this feeling is eclipsed, it is difficult to recognise.
Second, extending to the remaining feelings. As in the hell realms exclusive painful feeling co-arises, so too in the lower three meditative absorption heavens exclusive pleasant feeling co-arises; from the fourth absorption heaven up to the summit of existence, exclusive neutral feeling co-arises.

items.zh: 復次，阿賴耶識，或於一時與轉識相應善、不善、無記諸心所俱時而轉。如是阿賴耶識雖與轉識俱時而轉，亦與客受，客善、不善、無記心所俱時而轉，然不應說與彼相應。

blocks.text: How seeds become experience and experience becomes seeds, and the first appearance of manas, the self-grasping mind.

The store-consciousness serves the other consciousnesses as their seed and as their basis. Master Cháng Bǎi: active consciousness immediately plants seeds; frequent anger strengthens the seed of hatred.

Master Cháng Bǎi: throughout life, manas grasps the seeing part of the store-consciousness as a self. In the attainment of cessation, the manas that grasps a self does not operate, while the grasping of dharmas remains.
When all five senses are active, the sixth and seventh join as well. Master Cháng Bǎi: in meditation the five are still; only the sixth and seventh operate.
Master Cháng Bǎi: the key is removing defiled manas. Even giving remains contaminated while one still grasps at marks.

The innate neutral feeling is mixed with others. Master Cháng Bǎi: whatever the active feeling, the store-consciousness stays neutral; neutral feeling is only eclipsed by intense pain. The highest pleasure is in the third meditation; from the fourth up, feeling is neutral.
"Frequent anger strengthens the seed of hatred." This is the practical side of the theory: every moment of practice plants seeds, too.

quiz.q: Which two conditions does it provide the active consciousnesses?
quiz.why: As their seed and as their basis.

quiz.q: "Because manas serves as basis." What kind of basis does Master Cháng Bǎi call it?
options: the basis of defilement and purity, their root
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: manas is the basis of defilement and purity, their source.

quiz.q: "Nurturing seeds in the present life." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: frequent anger strengthens the seed of hatred
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: active consciousness immediately habituates seeds; frequent anger strengthens the seed of hatred.

quiz.q: When co-arising with only one, which is it?
quiz.why: Manas. Master Cháng Bǎi: throughout life manas grasps the seeing part of the store-consciousness as a self.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi define "states with and without mind"?
options: the six ceased or arisen; excluding final nirvāṇa; in cessation self-grasping manas doesn't operate
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: states depend on all six, excluding final nirvāṇa; in cessation self-grasping manas doesn't operate while dharma-grasping manas remains. The English names only the sixth.

quiz.q: When does it co-arise with seven?
options: when all five sense-consciousnesses are active together
quiz.why: When all five are active; the sixth and seventh join as well.

quiz.q: What situation does Master Cháng Bǎi give for co-arising with two?
options: in meditation, the five stop; only the sixth and seventh are active with it
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: in meditation the five are still; only the sixth and seventh operate.

quiz.q: "Bound by appearances." What is the key, and what is this bondage?
options: removing defiled manas; the seeing part bound by the seen part
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the key is removing defiled manas; the seeing part is bound by the seen part. Even giving remains contaminated while marks persist.

quiz.q: Among humans, how does its innate feeling co-arise with others?
options: the innate neutral feeling mixes with the active consciousnesses' feelings
quiz.why: The innate neutral feeling is mixed with others. Master Cháng Bǎi: whatever the active feeling, the store-consciousness stays neutral.

quiz.q: "Eclipsed by others." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say 他 is?
options: not other beings, but the intense suffering itself
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: neutral feeling is eclipsed by intense pain; the suffering itself is called "other." "Others" could suggest other beings.

quiz.q: Which feeling co-arises in the lower three absorption grounds?
quiz.why: Exclusive pleasure; from the fourth up, neutral. Master Cháng Bǎi: the highest pleasure is in the third.
